specs.source_title: Introduction to the modules and functions of AMS lite | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.quote: When all four slots have filaments inserted, AMS cannot determine which slot the filament is dispensed from based on the sensors alone.
specs.note: Same page: "The PTFE tubes corresponding to each slot of the AMS lite are connected to the filament hub, which holds the four tubes together." The store box lists "AMS lite Rotary Spool Holder (x4)".

specs.source_title: Connection Guide for Multiple AMS Units with Different Printer Models | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.quote: The AMS lite is only compatible with A series printers. Each A series printer supports only one AMS lite.
specs.note: The AMS lite intro agrees ("The A1 series printers can be connected to a single AMS lite"). On an A1 series printer it cannot be combined with other AMS models; the A2L takes up to 4 AMS units plus 1 AMS lite (A1 Series / A2L Connection Guide sections of the same page).

specs.value: Only compatible with A series printers; each A series printer supports only one AMS lite.
specs.source_title: Connection Guide for Multiple AMS Units with Different Printer Models | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.quote: The AMS lite is only compatible with A series printers. Each A series printer supports only one AMS lite.
specs.conflict_note: The store page row compat.statement (unverified, "compatibility section") holds feature prose about spools: "The spring loaded rotary spool holder grips the spool at the center hole, improving spool compatibility especially for those paper spools." It is not a printer compatibility statement. This official_doc row outranks it; the merge records the disagreement.
specs.note: The AMS lite intro adds: "AMS lite is unsuitable for use with X1 and P1 series printers." The store option value is "A1&A2 Series".

specs.source_title: Introduction to the modules and functions of AMS lite | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.quote: The A1 series printers can be connected to a single AMS lite, limiting its support to a maximum of 4-color printing.
specs.test_condition: One AMS lite on an A1 series printer
specs.note: On the A2L combined with 4 AMS units the AMS lite provides 3 feeding channels (A2L AMS Connection Guide, FAQ: "the AMS lite provides 3 feeding channels ... enabling up to 19-color printing").

specs.source_title: Introduction to the modules and functions of AMS lite | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: AMS lite feeding system › First stage feeder
specs.quote: Each slot in AMS lite is equipped with a feeder responsible for feeding the filament into or out of the tool head. The feeder includes a filament detection sensor
specs.note: Same page, "Filament run-out detection and filament backup function": the feeder's Hall switch is checked when the tool head detects run-out.

specs.source_title: Introduction to the modules and functions of AMS lite | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: AMS lite feeding system › First stage feeder
specs.quote: Each feeder is equipped with an odometer featuring a passive wheel.

specs.source_title: A2L AMS Connection Guide | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: A2L + 4 AMS + 1 AMS lite › Operation Steps › Step 5: Connect the AMS lite
specs.quote: Insert the cable into the two cable organizers, then plug it into the printer's 4-pin interface.
specs.note: Same page, Required Accessories › AMS and Cable: "AMS lite | 1 | Comes with a 4-pin cable". The store box lists "Bambu Bus Cable-4Pin".

specs.source_title: Bambu Lab AMS lite - Automatic Material System (store page)
specs.locator: AMS lite Tech Specs › row 7 (Supported Filament*¹)
specs.quote: PLA, PETG,ASA, PET, PA, PC, PVA (dry), BVOH (dry), PP, POM, HIPS and Bambu PLA-CF
specs.test_condition: Judged from loading/unloading only (table note *¹); printer compatibility is checked separately
specs.conflict_note: The page row parses as x.supported_filament_1 (the footnote marker "*¹" defeats the "Supported Filament" synonym); same items, this row types them. The wiki filament guide (AMS / AMS lite column) also names PLA Metal/Wood/Marble, PETG HF/Translucent, Support for PLA, PLA/PETG and PA/PET, and Bambu PA-CF / PAHT-CF as compatible, while its text says PLA Wood is not recommended for the AMS lite.

value: other brand filament that contains carbon fiber or glass fiber
specs.source_title: Bambu Lab AMS lite - Automatic Material System (store page)
specs.locator: AMS lite Tech Specs › row 9 (Unsupported Filament*³)
specs.quote: TPE, TPU, PVA (wet), BVOH (wet), Bambu PET-CF / PA6-CF / TPU 95A and other brand filament that contains carbon fiber or glass fiber
specs.test_condition: Too soft, too brittle or too abrasive for the AMS lite (table note *³)
specs.conflict_note: The page row parses as x.unsupported_filament_3 (footnote marker "*³"); same items, here "Bambu PET-CF / PA6-CF / TPU 95A" is three items. The wiki filament guide agrees on TPU and PET-CF/GF (Not Compatible) and adds PPA-CF/GF and PPS-CF/GF. Not the "Not Recommended Filament*²" row (Bambu PLA Glow, Bambu PETG-CF, generic glow PLA), which has no registry key and stays x.not_recommended_filament_2; the wiki also marks ABS and ABS-GF "AMS lite: Not Recommended".
